scope_note: Each edge is judged against the generic sense of the `to` row (its name and its generic synonyms). Where a `to` row also folds in specific kinds as synonyms (bread: baguette, whole wheat bread; cereal: puffed cereal, cheerios), a line that names one of those kinds is a table-merge issue, not an edge issue, and is not used to reject an edge. This applies to every family in the same way.

standard_by_family.bread: Usable only if `from` is a leavened loaf bread of the kind the `bread` row covers (white, sandwich, sourdough, french, italian, baguette); rolls, pastries, flatbreads and other distinct bread products are substitutes.
standard_by_family.chili: The `chili_pepper` row covers the generic green or red chili, fresh or dried, including small dried red chiles; usable only for a small, thin-walled hot chili of the bird's-eye / arbol type that fills that line without changing heat or flavour; large mild chiles, very hot fruity chiles and distinctive dried Mexican or Peruvian chiles are substitutes.
standard_by_family.cheese: The `cheese` row covers grated, shredded or sliced cheese; usable for a firm or semi-firm cheese that can be grated, shredded or sliced and melts; soft-ripened, fresh unripened, non-melting, crumbly-topping and snack forms are substitutes or unsure.
standard_by_family.onion: The `onion` row covers fresh bulb onions; usable for another fresh bulb onion; dried, pasted or fried onion products are substitutes.
standard_by_family.processed_form: A processed form (paste, powder, flakes) is usable only when the `to` row's own synonyms already cover that processed form (coffee: instant coffee, instant espresso); otherwise it is a substitute for the fresh item (garlic, ginger, onion).
standard_by_family.fish: The `fish` row covers fresh fish (whole, steak, cleaned); preserved fish (dried, smoked, stockfish) is a substitute.
standard_by_family.produce_kind: A named variety is usable only if a cook would use it in the generic line with no change in texture or cooking; asian pear (stays crisp), daikon (row means small salad radish; `white radish` maps to daikon) and ragi (mostly sold as flour) fail or are unsure; edamame is green immature soybean, not the dried soybean the row covers.
standard_by_family.cereal: Judged against the generic `cereal` / `breakfast cereal` / `dry cereal` line, as bread is judged against its generic line; a common ready-to-eat breakfast cereal meets it.
